questions.prompt: Prove that √2 is irrational.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms. Squaring gives p² = 2q², so p is even. Put p = 2k; then q² = 2k², so q is even too. This contradicts gcd(p,q) = 1. Hence √2 is irrational.

markingScheme.criterion: Assume √2 = p/q in lowest terms and square
Show p is even and then q is even

questions.prompt: Prove that √3 is irrational.

answerKey.modelAnswer: Assume √3 = p/q in lowest terms. Then p² = 3q², so 3 divides p. Write p = 3k; substitution gives q² = 3k², so 3 divides q. This contradicts coprimality. Therefore √3 is irrational.

markingScheme.criterion: Show 3 divides p and then q

questions.prompt: For 5, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 10, 10, 12, find the median and mode.

answerKey.modelAnswer: There are 9 observations. The 5th value is 9, so median = 9. The most frequent value is 10, so mode = 10.

questions.prompt: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 2 cm and AE = 6 cm, find EC.

answerKey.modelAnswer: By BPT, AD/DB = AE/EC. Thus 3/2 = 6/EC, so EC = 4 cm.

questions.prompt: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC. If AD = 4 cm, DB = 6 cm and AC = 15 cm, find AE.

answerKey.modelAnswer: By BPT, AE:EC = AD:DB = 2:3. Since AC = 15 cm, AE = (2/5)×15 = 6 cm.

questions.prompt: State the AA similarity criterion and explain why two triangles with two pairs of equal corresponding angles are similar.

answerKey.modelAnswer: If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another, the third angles are also equal because the angle sum is 180°. The triangles are similar by AA.

markingScheme.criterion: State the two equal corresponding angles
Use the angle sum to infer the third pair

questions.prompt: State the SSS similarity criterion. Show that triangles with sides 3, 4, 5 cm and 6, 8, 10 cm are similar.

answerKey.modelAnswer: The corresponding side ratios are 3/6 = 4/8 = 5/10 = 1/2. Hence the triangles are similar by SSS.

questions.prompt: A student claims that moving farther from a fixed tower makes its angle of elevation larger. Evaluate the claim using tan θ = height/distance.

answerKey.modelAnswer: The claim is incorrect. For fixed height h, increasing the distance d decreases h/d, so the acute angle θ decreases.

markingScheme.criterion: State that the claim is incorrect

Conclude that angle of elevation decreases

questions.prompt: Two observers view the same tower from level ground. A is 10 m away and B is 20 m away. Compare their angles of elevation.

answerKey.modelAnswer: For tower height h, tan θA = h/10 and tan θB = h/20. Thus tan θA > tan θB, so θA > θB.
